newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil cargoes firm, weather dampens barges.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil cargoes firm, weather dampens barges.

text.p: NWE gas oil cargo premiums were unchanged to firm in busy early discussion on Friday but barges remained listless on slack demand dampened by continuing mild winter weather, traders said.
Benchmark Feb IPE gas oil futures lost $5.50 to $202.50 a tonne at 1315 GMT, following easier Brent in thin screen trade.
Traders said tightness in low sulphur helped support premiums with delivery for prompt to the first 10 days of February assessed at around Feb IPE +$16/18.
German winter grade heating oil cargoes were bid at Feb IPE +$ and offered around +$7.50/8 cif Hamburg.

French quality was around Feb IPE +$6 cif Le Havre for Feb 1-10, with prompt a very notional Feb IPE +$9/11. Russians were talked around the Feb IPE +$7 level done on Thursday but remain under pressure from abundant supply.
Barges were stagnant again on listless German demand. Refinery grade 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil was done 50 cents easier at Feb IPE +$3 for Feb 1-10 and +$4 for prompt.
Low sulphur diesel was around Feb IPE +$13/14, about 50 cents firmer on tighter supply. Demand remains modest.
